[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Privacy"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- Events, snapshots, contracts and health cards live in `$DSH_HOME/firewall/`. **No telemetry.**
- T"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"he only outbound path is a webhook **you** configure. It is off by default, sends red-line
events on"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"ly — never the full timeline, never file contents, never credentials. The audit
report records only "},{"id":"p16s4","text":"the webhook's origin (scheme + host), never the URL with any token in it.
- The plugin holds itself "},{"id":"p16s5","text":"to its own standard: no credential access, no silent network. Its own
capability surface, as scanned"},{"id":"p16s6","text":" by its own health card, is part of the test suite."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## Limitations"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"Stated plainly, because a security tool that overstates its coverage is worse than none:"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"- **Heuristic, not a proof.** A static scan cannot see credentials injected at runtime; that is
what"},{"id":"p19s2","text":" the runtime layer is for. On 154 real ecosystem plugins the static pass recalls 66.1 % at
17.2 % fa"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"lse positives. Being listed on a plugin marketplace is not a security review, and
neither is this RE"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"ADME: treat every plugin, including this one, as untrusted until observed.
- **Not an adversarial sa"},{"id":"p19s5","text":"ndbox.** A plugin that deliberately targets the instrumentation
(native modules, `process.binding`, "},{"id":"p19s6","text":"patching the probe) can evade it. The goal is continuous,
attributable visibility.
- **Attribution n"},{"id":"p19s7","text":"eeds the launcher.** Without `dsh-pdr` (or another host-level preload), the
in-plugin probe installs"},{"id":"p19s8","text":" too late and attribution collapses — measured **0 of 3** on a real
session with everything falling "},{"id":"p19s9","text":"back to `host`. The DSH **Desktop app cannot be launched
through the launcher**, so its sessions are"},{"id":"p19s10","text":" currently outside attribution; the health card and
the offline `audit` / `aggregate` commands are u"},{"id":"p19s11","text":"naffected. A host-level `--import` hook is the
tracked next step.
- **Known gaps** — named imports o"},{"id":"p19s12","text":"f `child_process` / `http` / `net` when the facade predates the
probe. `fs` is covered on both hook "},{"id":"p19s13","text":"layers.
- **The trial install is an isolated child process, not a sandbox.** It gets a temp `DSH_HOM"},{"id":"p19s14","text":"E`,
a hard timeout and SIGKILL on hang, so a crashing or hung plugin cannot take the host down —
but"},{"id":"p19s15","text":" a plugin is still running with your user's privileges inside it.
- **In-host web mount is unverifie"},{"id":"p19s16","text":"d.** The `dsh-h3` adapter follows a contract measured on a live
community plugin and is covered by 1"},{"id":"p19s17","text":"1 injected-runtime assertions, but `dsh-h3` is a Typert
virtual module that cannot be resolved offli"},{"id":"p19s18","text":"ne. Until it is verified in a live host the panel
falls back to `serve.js`.
